text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Grenade-throwing youths sack villages in continuing clashes as feuding over relocation of local council headquarters shifts to Koko near oil town of Warri.
- Army to hold training exercises from Monday in the northern town of Kontagora to test its combat readiness, says spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Felix Chukwuma.
- Headquarters of First Bank of Nigeria Plc and DN Meyer Nigeria Plc sealed off by Lagos state to recover tax of 99 million naira owed the state.

- Nigerian government pays cash calls, its own share in the funding of its joint venture operations with multinational operations, as the companies open escrow accounts for the money as directed by the authorities.
- Government orders arrest of masterminds of the clashes in oil town of Warri in the midwest, police sources say.
- Ministers of communications in Anglophone West Africa end seminar in Nigeria's capital Abuja dealing with the internet; call for deregulation of telecommunications in the region.
- Shell oil company may start drilling for oil in the Gongola basin in northern Nigeria, company sources say.
- Federal government may apply tough sanctions to check spurious demands for foreign exchange at weekly auction, says industries minister Lieutenant-General Mohammed Haladu.
